ety.text: From joke + -er, but in the sense of a playing card possibly by alteration of German Jucker, also the origin of the name of the card game euchre.

senses.d: A playing card that features a picture of a joker (that is, a jester) and that may be used as a wild card in some card games.
Something kept in reserve that can be used to gain an advantage; a trump card.
ex: Rebus decided to use their joker. 'Mr Lintz made a phone call to this office. He was talking for over twenty minutes.'
Some joker keeps throwing eggs at my windows.
Don't waste your breath on these jokers round here.

senses.d: A clause in a contract that undermines its apparent provisions.
ex: Then, sir, on page 12 of the agreement there is a joker clause, which provides for payments in addition to the ten per cent, […]

senses.d: A friendly unit that acts as a suspected hostile unit in a military excercise.
ex: Joker - A friendly track or contact acting as a "suspect" track for exercise purposes only. (STANAG 1241)

From Latin iocus (“joke, jest, pastime”), from Proto-Italic *jokos (“word, (playful?) saying”), from Proto-Indo-European *yokos (“word, utterance”), from ultimate root Proto-Indo-European *yek- (“to speak, utter”) (of which distant cognates include Proto-Celtic *yextis (“language”) (Breton yezh (“language”) and Welsh iaith (“language”)) and German Beichte (“confession”)). Cognate with French jeu, Italian gioco, Portuguese jogo, Spanish juego, Romanian joc, English Yule, Danish Jule, Norwegian Bokmål Jul, Swedish Jul, and Norwegian Nynorsk jol.

ex: Or witty joke our airy senses moves / To pleasant laughter.

senses.d: Something said or done for amusement, not in seriousness.
A laughably worthless thing or person; a sham.
ex: Your effort at cleaning your room is a joke.

senses.d: Something that is far easier or far less challenging than expected.
ex: The final exam was a joke.

senses.d: To do or say something for amusement rather than seriously.
ex: I didn’t mean what I said — I was only joking.

senses.d: To dupe in a friendly manner for amusement; to mess with, play with.
ex: Relax, man, I'm just joking with you.

senses.d: To make merry with; to make jokes upon; to rally.
